'''Kazimierz Marcinkiewicz'''{{efn|{{IPA|pl|kaˈʑimjɛʂ mart͡ɕiŋˈkʲɛvit͡ʂ|-|Pl-Kazimierz Marcinkiewicz.ogg}}}} (born 20 December 1959) is a Polish conservative politician who served as [[Prime Minister of Poland]] from 31 October 2005 to 14 July 2006. He was a member of the [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] party (''Prawo i Sprawiedliwość'', PiS).

== Early life ==
Born in [[Gorzów Wielkopolski]], Marcinkiewicz graduated in 1984 from the Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry (having studied [[physics]]) of the [[Wrocław University]]. He  also completed post-graduate course in Administration at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University]] in [[Poznań]]. He worked as an elementary school teacher and a headmaster in his homecity of Gorzów Wielkopolski.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marcinkiewicz.org/zyciorys |title=Życiorys |access-date=24 November 2019}}</ref>

In the 1980s he was also a member of the [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]] movement and editor of underground press materials. In 1992 he became a State Secretary (formal name for deputy minister) in the Ministry of National Education. From 1999 to 2000 he was the cabinet chief for Prime Minister [[Jerzy Buzek]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marcinkiewicz.org/zyciorys |title=Życiorys |access-date=24 November 2019}}</ref>

== Prime Minister of Poland == 
{{Main|Cabinet of Kazimierz Marcinkiewicz}}
Following the victory of the Law and Justice party in the [[2005 Polish parliamentary election|September 2005 Polish parliamentary elections]], its prime ministerial candidate, party leader [[Jarosław Kaczyński]] decided against becoming prime minister so as not to damage the chances of his twin brother, [[Lech Kaczyński]] in the then-upcoming [[2005 Polish presidential election|October presidential election]]. Instead the little-known Marcinkiewicz [[Marcinkiewicz government|became PM]], leading a coalition formed by Jarosław, who remained in the background, but influential.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marcinkiewicz.org/zyciorys |title=Życiorys |access-date=24 November 2019}}</ref>

Before his prime ministerial appointment, Marcinkiewicz remained a political cipher, which resulted in a political [[blank cheque|carte blanche]] after the appointment. Relatively unknown to the public at that time, due to his intensive political activity Marcinkiewicz gained a high public recognition, rapidly becoming the most trusted and popular politician in Poland.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tygodnikprzeglad.pl/zagadka-marcinkiewicza/ |title=Zagadka Marcinkiewicza |access-date=24 November 2019}}</ref>
{{Politics of Poland}}
Marcinkiewicz strongly supported Polish membership in EU, although he disagreed with several more integrationist ideas, such as the [[European Constitution]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2007}} Economic policy of his cabinet is a continuation of those conducted by previous governments.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pb.pl/po-odejsciu-gilowskiej-rzad-zachowa-kotwice-budzetowa-i-plany-reform-321579 |language=pl |title=Po odejściu Gilowskiej rząd zachowa kotwicę budżetową i plany reform |website=pb.pl |date=23 June 2006 |access-date=11 November 2023}}</ref>

Following speculations of a rift with [[Jarosław Kaczyński]], Marcinkiewicz tendered his resignation on 7 July 2006, maintaining however that no one will insert a wedge between him and Kaczyński, words he directed at [[Donald Tusk]].<ref>
{{cite news
 |url          = https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/5159994.stm
 |title        = Poland's prime minister resigns
 |publisher    = BBC News
 |date         = 7 July 2006
 |access-date  = 14 July 2006
 |url-status   = live|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081219134552/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/5159994.stm
 |archive-date = 19 December 2008
}}</ref> He was succeeded as prime minister by Kaczyński.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/5165214.stm |title=Poland leader's twin named as PM |website=bbc.co.uk |date=10 July 2006 |access-date=11 November 2023}}</ref>

== Later life ==
On 18 July Marcinkiewicz was appointed as the temporary acting mayor of [[Warsaw]], a so-called "comissar".
During the municipal elections in 2006, he was the [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] candidate for mayor of Warsaw. In the first round of voting, held on 12 November, he got 38.42%, while his closest rival, [[Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz]] of the opposition [[Civic Platform]] won 34.15% of the votes. In the second round, held on 26 November, he got 46.82% of the votes, losing the election.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://wybory2006.pkw.gov.pl/kbw/wynikiWbp2Tura4916.html?id=146501 |language=pl |title=Wybory Prezydenta Miasta - głosowanie ponowne |website=pkw.gov.pl |access-date=11 November 2023}}</ref>

He was one of the directors of the [[European Bank for Reconstruction and Development]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ebrd.com/about/structure/direct.htm |title=Management & structure > Directors of the EBRD |work=EBRD.com |publisher=[[European Bank for Reconstruction and Development]] |access-date=2007-07-27 |url-status = dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070714010416/http://www.ebrd.com/about/structure/direct.htm |archive-date=2007-07-14 }}</ref> from March 2007 until May 2008.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

From 2008 until 2013 he worked for [[Goldman Sachs]], presumably as a lobbyist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvn24.pl/wiadomosci-z-kraju,3/marcinkiewicz-nie-pracuje-juz-dla-goldman-sachs,300871.html|title=Marcinkiewicz nie pracuje już dla Goldman Sachs|language=pl|trans-title=Marcinkiewicz no longer works for Goldman Sachs|date=18 January 2013|website=TVN24.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920014437/http://www.tvn24.pl/wiadomosci-z-kraju,3/marcinkiewicz-nie-pracuje-juz-dla-goldman-sachs,300871.html|archive-date=20 September 2016}}</ref> Despite his work for Goldman Sachs, major Polish newspapers and news television channels, informed that former Polish prime minister barely spoke English after one year spent in London. He could not answer simple questions asked by Warsaw based English native speakers hired by one of the Polish tabloid who called him to offer a job in other bank in UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvn24.pl/wiadomosci-z-kraju,3/do-you-speak-english-no-no-no,57602.html|title=&quot;Do you speak English? No, no, no&quot;|language=pl|date=8 May 2008|website=TVN24.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122163454/http://www.tvn24.pl/wiadomosci-z-kraju,3/do-you-speak-english-no-no-no,57602.html|archive-date=22 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://wiadomosci.dziennik.pl/polityka/artykuly/75217,marcinkiewicz-po-angielsku-aaa-yyy.html|title=Marcinkiewicz po angielsku: "Aaa... yyy..."|language=pl|trans-title=Marcinkiewicz in English: "Uhh... umm..."|date=8 May 2008|website=Dziennik.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122155650/http://wiadomosci.dziennik.pl/polityka/artykuly/75217,marcinkiewicz-po-angielsku-aaa-yyy.html|archive-date=22 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fakt.pl/wydarzenia/polityka/marcinkiewicz-duka-po-angielsku/3e643f7|title=Marcinkiewicz duka po angielsku. A pracował w Londynie!|language=pl|trans-title=Marcinkiewicz stammers in English. And he has worked in London!|date=6 February 2014|website=fakt.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122222130/http://www.fakt.pl/wydarzenia/polityka/marcinkiewicz-duka-po-angielsku/3e643f7|archive-date=22 November 2016}}</ref>

In 2009, after divorcing his wife and mother of four, he married his former mistress, 22 years his junior,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvn24.pl/ciekawostki-michalki,5/tajny-slub-marcinkiewicza-z-nbsp-isabel-w-barcelonie,108315.html|title=Tajny ślub Marcinkiewicza z&nbsp;Isabel w Barcelonie?|language=pl|trans-title=Secret wedding of Marcinkiewicz and Isabel in Barcelona|date=9 September 2009|website=TVN24.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920014535/http://www.tvn24.pl/ciekawostki-michalki,5/tajny-slub-marcinkiewicza-z-nbsp-isabel-w-barcelonie,108315.html|archive-date=20 September 2016}}</ref> with whom he was embroiled in a bitter divorce battle in September 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fakt.pl/polityka/marcinkiewicz-rozwodzi-sie-z-isabel-rozwod-marcinkiewiczow-,artykuly,571575.html|title=Pikantne szczegóły związku Marcinkiewicza z Isabel|language=pl|trans-title=Spicy details about Marcinkiewicz and Isabel relationship|date=8 September 2015|website=fakt.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305041835/http://www.fakt.pl/polityka/marcinkiewicz-rozwodzi-sie-z-isabel-rozwod-marcinkiewiczow-,artykuly,571575.html|archive-date=5 March 2016}}</ref>

== Criticism ==
In the first half of 2009, he came under heavy criticism because of not keeping up with the moral values he promoted while being engaged in politics. In particular, it was discovered that he was criticizing extra-marital affairs and praising traditional family values, while having an affair himself.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dziennik.pl/opinie/article327623/Marcinkiewicz_i_zlamane_sumienie.html|title=Marcinkiewicz i złamane sumienie|language=pl|trans-title=Marcinkiewicz and broken conscience|work=Dziennik.pl|date=24 February 2009|access-date=2009-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301100918/http://www.dziennik.pl/opinie/article327623/Marcinkiewicz_i_zlamane_sumienie.html|archive-date=2009-03-01}}</ref>

== Famous quotes ==
He became famous for his enthusiastic "Yes, yes, yes!" after the success in negotiations of the EU budget on 17 December 2005,<ref>{{cite AV media|url=http://w165.wrzuta.pl/audio/35wJRsvATOc/marcinkiewicz_-_yes_yes_yes|title=Marcinkiewicz - Yes! Yes! Yes!|via=Wrzuta.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525152928/http://w165.wrzuta.pl/audio/35wJRsvATOc/marcinkiewicz_-_yes_yes_yes|archive-date=25 May 2017}}<!-- yes, there is archive URL, but it's unhelpful --></ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://politbiuro.gazeta.pl/politbiuro/51,85402,5761561.html?i=1|title='Yes, yes, yes!' - tak cieszył się premier Marcinkiewicz po udanych negocjacjach na szczycie UE|website=politbiuro.gazeta.pl|access-date=2012-10-21}}{{Dead link|fix-attempted=yes|date=July 2019}}</ref> – the phrase that has entered into the Polish popular culture as a symbol of a political success 'with a human face' (not refraining from real emotions),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wyborcza.pl/1,76842,3072621.html|title=Marcinkiewicz o budżecie UE: yes, yes, yes!|language=pl|trans-title=Marcinkiewicz on the EU budget: yes, yes, yes!|first1=Konrad|last1=Niklewicz|first2=Jacek|last2=Pawlicki|website=Wyborcza.pl|date=2005-12-17|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110512071227/http://wyborcza.pl/1,76842,3072621.html|archive-date=12 May 2011}}</ref> but at the same time as a symbol of untempered self-confidence. As a rhetorical device ([[epizeuxis]]), it has already been re-used by [[Volkswagen]] in its publicity campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wiadomosci.gazeta.pl/wiadomosci/1,55670,3226296.html|title=Słownik IV RP|language=pl|trans-title=Political vocabulary of the 4th Republic of Poland|website=Gazeta.pl|access-date=9 December 2017|url-status = dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214110941/http://wiadomosci.gazeta.pl/wiadomosci/1,55670,3226296.html|archive-date=14 February 2012}}</ref>
